description: Icon glyphs from the bundled 'icomoon' icon font. Every glyph is exposed as a class following the convention `icon-<name>` (e.g. icon-search, icon-edit). The shared selector `[class^="icon-"], [class*=" icon-"]` applies the icomoon font-family and rendering, and each individual `.icon-<name>:before` injects the glyph via a content code point. Apply an icon class to an empty inline element (typically a <span> or <i>). There is no separate base class — the icon-* class is sufficient. The font ships HUNDREDS of glyphs; consult src/scss/vendors/icomoon.scss for the authoritative list rather than guessing names.

always: Use the literal `icon-<name>` class for an existing glyph defined in icomoon.scss; the [class^="icon-"] selector then supplies the font.
Place the icon on its own inline element (span or i) with no text content — the glyph comes from the ::before pseudo-element.
Many icons ship as an outline + a `-fill` solid pair (e.g. icon-bell / icon-bell-fill); pick the appropriate weight.
never: Do not invent icon names — only classes literally present in icomoon.scss render a glyph.
Do not put visible text inside the icon element.
Do not omit accessibility handling (see a11y).

a11y: Decorative icons must be hidden from assistive tech with aria-hidden="true".
An icon that is the only content of an interactive control (icon-only button/link) needs an accessible name via aria-label on the control.
A meaningful standalone icon should provide a text alternative (e.g. role="img" + aria-label).
